doc.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Clark Terry's individuality and Sweets Edison
summary: Wendell and Monk discuss Clark Terry's unmistakable licks and compare Sweets Edison.

blocks.x: You know when — I don’t know how you put it into words, but you hear those, like he was playing some riffs, it was the first set before he played, and Harry Allen would pick them up. But these riffs he came up with were so uniquely him.

And they would take this little turn like gee if I had thought of that I would not have been able to think of that cool little way he ended that thing you know. And it’s just the years. I guess it’s the years. And his personality.
Yeah it’s just him. I mean he just — what comes out of his horn is purely Clark Terry. And nobody — I mean there are very few people in history like that. I mean purely. I © Fillius Jazz Archive -12-

mean when you hear Sweets Edison there’s no doubt. I mean Charlie Shavers and him played a little bit alike. But when you actually hear Sweets Edison there’s no doubt who it is [scats]. I mean you know it’s coming and you’re still so pleased when it happens. And that’s the way it was with Clark. Because he’d have some licks going on, and just the way he would end it was so [scats]. And it would just leave you hanging like, boy, man. I hope that happens to me one day, that I can just do that like that. I mean it’s easy to follow in some ways but to create it is another story.
